an6.62:3.2: “Sir, together with several mendicants I went to the Aciravatī River to bathe.
an6.62:3.3: When I had bathed and emerged from the water I stood in one robe drying my limbs.
an6.62:3.4: Then, sir, a certain mendicant went up to me and said to me,
an6.62:3.5: ‘Reverend Ānanda, when the Buddha declared that Devadatta was
an6.62:3.6: going to a place of loss, to hell, there to remain for an eon, irredeemable, did he do so after wholeheartedly deliberating, or was this just a way of speaking?’
an6.62:3.7: When he said this, sir, I said to that mendicant,
an6.62:3.8: ‘You’re right, reverend, that’s how the Buddha declared it.’”
an6.62:7.11: ‘Both skillful and unskillful qualities are found in this individual.’
an6.62:7.12: After some time I encompass their mind and understand:
an6.62:7.13: ‘The skillful qualities of this individual have vanished, but the unskillful qualities are still present.
an6.62:7.14: Nevertheless, their skillful root is unbroken, and from that the skillful will appear.
an6.62:8.11: ‘Both skillful and unskillful qualities are found in this individual.’
an6.62:8.12: After some time I encompass their mind and understand:
an6.62:8.13: ‘The unskillful qualities of this individual have vanished, but the skillful qualities are still present.
an6.62:8.14: Nevertheless, their unskillful root is unbroken, and from that the unskillful will appear.
an6.62:8.17: And this is how the Realized One knows a person’s faculties by encompassing their mind.
an6.62:8.18: And this is how the Realized One knows the future origination of a person’s qualities by encompassing their mind.
